sources.title: Afghanistan Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: The State Department's live Afghanistan guidance addresses U.S.-citizen entry requirements and warns that Afghan immigration may reject visas issued by some overseas missions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Afghan immigration officials may refuse to accept visas that were issued by Afghan Republic-era officials.

sources.title: Burkina Faso Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: The State Department's current Burkina Faso travel guidance expressly reports the destination government's U.S.-national visa suspension and its effective date.
sources.supportingExcerpt: As of Dec 30, 2025, the Government of Burkina Faso suspended visas to Americans with limited exceptions.

sources.title: Chad Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: The State Department's current Chad entry section expressly says U.S. citizens need a visa but are not routinely being issued one, and excludes arrival issuance.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Government of Chad is not routinely issuing visas to U.S. citizens at this time.

sources.title: Iran Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: The State Department's live Iran guidance states the tourist-visa requirement but does not give an ordinary U.S.-passport issuance mode.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A tourist visa is required, except for Kish Island.

sources.title: Mali Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: The State Department's current Mali entry section expressly reports the destination government's U.S.-citizen visa-issuance suspension and its effective date.
sources.supportingExcerpt: As of January 1, 2026, the government of Mali suspended visa issuance to U.S. citizens.

sources.title: North Korea Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: The State Department's live North Korea guidance says an ordinary U.S. passport is invalid for the trip without a narrowly granted special validation.
sources.supportingExcerpt: U.S. passports are not valid for travel into or through North Korea unless they contain a special validation.

sources.title: Israel, the West Bank, and Gaza International Travel Information
sources.jurisdiction: United States / Israel, West Bank and Gaza
sources.officialityEvidence: The State Department's live entry guidance distinguishes Israeli ETA-IL travel to the West Bank from Gaza access, Palestinian registration, and crossing-specific treatment.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All persons seeking to enter or depart Israel, the West Bank, or Gaza are subject to immigration and security screening.

sources.title: Trinidad and Tobago Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: The State Department's live Trinidad and Tobago travel-requirements section expressly states the ordinary U.S.-visitor short-stay visa rule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No visa is required for 90 days or less.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: Trinidad and Tobago short visitor waiver
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance establishes visa-free Trinidad and Tobago visitor access for ordinary U.S. passports for stays of 90 days or less.
conditions: Applies to a current ordinary U.S. passport for a visitor stay of 90 days or less.
The State Department says the passport must have at least six months' validity beyond arrival or the stay duration and one blank page per stamp.
Work, residence, dual-national, special-document, child-travel, carrier, health, security and final-admission rules remain outside this classification.

conflicts.explanation: Current State Department guidance says Burkina Faso suspended visas to Americans from 30 December 2025, with limited exceptions. This cannot be represented as a functioning ordinary visitor eVisa route.

conflicts.officialStatus: unavailable (not routinely issuing visas to U.S. citizens)
conflicts.explanation: Current State Department guidance says Chad is not routinely issuing visas to U.S. citizens and that visas are unavailable on arrival. The fallback advance-visa status does not describe current ordinary issuance.

Current State Department guidance says Mali suspended visa issuance to U.S. citizens from 1 January 2026, with limited exceptions. This cannot be represented as a functioning ordinary advance-visa route.

unresolved.reason: Current State Department guidance requires an Afghan visa before travel but says immigration officials may reject visas from some overseas missions. A working ordinary U.S.-passport visitor issuance channel is not established.

Current State Department guidance says a tourist visa is required except for Kish Island but does not establish ordinary U.S.-passport issuance timing or a nationwide visitor route. No complement is inferred.

A normal U.S. passport is invalid for North Korea travel without narrowly granted special validation; the page also does not establish ordinary tourist-visa issuance timing. The taxonomy has no passport-invalid or entry-unavailable status.

Current U.S. guidance separates ETA-IL access to Israel and the West Bank from Gaza closure, Palestinian population-registration and crossing controls. It does not establish one ordinary U.S.-passport status for the exact PS destination scope.
